articles.title: Accidentally Accused Michael Bisping of Hiring Hookers #ufc
articles.description: Chael Sonnen shares one of the most embarrassing—and funniest—stories of his broadcasting career. It all started with a misunderstanding over the word **"slapper,"** which in the UK can be used as slang for a prostitute. Trying to make a joke on air, Chael accidentally dragged Michael Bisping into the story before immediately realizing what he'd just implied. Instead of moving on, Chael admits he made the situation even worse by trying to explain himself... over and over again. Eventually, Chael decided the only thing to do was tell Bisping the story in person. Much to his relief, the former UFC middleweight champion couldn't stop laughing and brushed it off with the perfect response. It's a classic Chael Sonnen story about live television, thinking on your feet, and how sometimes the harder you try to fix a mistake, the funnier it becomes. #ChaelSonnen #MichaelBisping #UFC #MMA #FunnyMoments #MMAStories #UFCNews #PodcastClips

articles.title: Ian Garry CAN Beat Islam Makhachev #ufc
articles.description: Can Ian Machado Garry really beat Islam Makhachev? Chael Sonnen isn't predicting the upset just yet—but he believes fans are making a mistake by acting like Ian has no chance. Chael explains why Garry's wrestling defense is far better than critics give him credit for, pointing to his performance against Shavkat Rakhmonov as evidence. If Ian can consistently defend takedowns and maintain his pace for a full 25 minutes, he has the tools to make life difficult for the UFC lightweight champion. Of course, Islam Makhachev remains one of the most complete fighters in the sport. His wrestling, conditioning, and championship experience make him an enormous challenge for anyone. But Chael argues this matchup deserves more respect than many fans are giving it. Ian Garry has even compared the potential fight to a modern version of Conor McGregor vs. José Aldo—a bold statement that raises the stakes even higher. Could Ian Garry pull off one of the biggest wins in recent UFC history? Chael breaks down exactly why he believes it's possible. #IanGarry #IslamMakhachev #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCNews #ShavkatRakhmonov #MMAAnalysis

articles.title: Will We Ever Have Another Conor McGregor? #ufc
articles.description: Will the UFC ever have another Conor McGregor? Chael Sonnen has a definitive answer: **No.** Chael explains why Conor McGregor was truly one of one — not just because of his ability to fight, but because he mastered every part of being a superstar. The fame, the entertainment, the professionalism, the personality, and the ability to turn every moment into an event made Conor something the sport may never see again. But Chael also points out something fans often overlook when a massive star leaves the sport: **the fans don't disappear.** They simply move on and find someone else to support. The UFC will always have new stars. The real challenge is finding the one athlete capable of capturing the attention of an entire generation and bringing all those fans along for the ride. Conor McGregor did exactly that. There will never be another Conor. But Chael believes there will be another superstar — and he's looking forward to seeing who becomes the next one. #ConorMcGregor #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #UFCStars #MMAHistory #UFCNews #CombatSports

articles.title: Arman vs Oliveira but what about with Gaethje? #ufc
articles.description: Arman Tsarukyan vs. Charles Oliveira for the BMF title could be the perfect solution for the UFC's lightweight division — and Chael Sonnen explains why. Chael believes Arman is a legitimate number-one contender, but with the BMF title sitting right there at lightweight, a matchup with Oliveira suddenly makes too much sense. It gives Arman a massive fight while taking another contender off the board and completely reshaping what's next for Justin Gaethje. So who does Gaethje fight next? A rematch with Paddy Pimblett doesn't seem likely. Ilia Topuria may not be ready to jump right back into another title fight. A Max Holloway rematch is possible, but Gaethje has reportedly expressed interest in something new. Chael believes the lightweight division may ultimately come down to Paddy or Ilia trying to take the belt from Gaethje — and one of them could be the final opponent of Gaethje's career. The question is simple: **Which fighter is best equipped to take the title from Justin Gaethje?** #ArmanTsarukyan #CharlesOliveira #JustinGaethje #UFC #MMA #ChaelSonnen #BMF #PaddyPimblett #IliaTopuria #UFCAnalysis

articles.title: 20 Years Ago Today, The WEC Named A Card After Our Founder 🔥🔥
articles.description: Twenty years ago today, the WEC named a card after a man who never fought a day in his life. He founded this site. Ryan Bennett co-founded MMAWeekly.com. Before Zuffa bought the WEC, he was its play-by-play voice. He was the guy holding the microphone in the cage after UFC 33 through 40. And every day he hosted MMAWeekly Radio alongside Frank Trigg. If you followed this sport in the early 2000s, you heard Ryan whether you knew his name or not. On May 31, 2006, he was driving his family across Utah on I-15. The vehicle went off the road. His wife and all four of his children survived. Ryan was killed instantly. He was 35. Two months later the WEC put his name on the card — WEC 22, July 28, 2006. Wes Sims was offered a bigger payday somewhere else that same weekend. He turned it down. In his own words in this video: "You can't put a price tag on friendship." Then he opened the fight with a flying drop kick — because that was the one thing Ryan had asked him for, over and over, for years. He finished it in 28 seconds. And on that same card, a young Brazilian named Glover Teixeira choked his opponent out in under 90 seconds. Fifteen years later he'd be UFC light heavyweight champion of the world. One night in a casino ballroom in Lemoore, California, for the guy who spent his whole life pointing a microphone at everybody else. articles.title: THIS DAY in MMA - JULY 27 🔥
articles.description: THIS DAY in MMA - JULY 27 🔥 2024 — Belal Muhammad walks into Leon Edwards' hometown of Manchester and takes his welterweight title. Nine takedowns in front of 17,000 people who came to boo him. 2019 — Cris Cyborg beats Felicia Spencer at UFC 240. Nobody in that building knew they'd just watched her last fight in the UFC. Six days later she was released. 2013 — Demetrious Johnson armbars John Moraga with 77 seconds left in the fifth round. His first ever finish in the Octagon, and the latest finish in UFC history at the time. 1997 — Mark Kerr makes his UFC debut at UFC 14 and wins the entire heavyweight tournament in ONE night. They called him The Smashing Machine. Almost 30 years later, Dwayne Johnson played him on screen. Same date. articles.title: Security Guard Asked Me for a UFC Fight
articles.description: Not every favor is meant to be cashed in. Chael shares the story of a security guard who believed one good deed had earned him a shot in the UFC—and why that's not how opportunity works. From the outside, it might seem like success comes from knowing the right people. In reality, every fighter still has to prove they belong. This story isn't just about one security guard. It's about networking, entitlement, earning opportunities, and the biggest mistake people make when trying to break into the fight business. Do connections matter? Absolutely. But they only open the door. What you do after that determines whether you stay in the room. Do you agree with Chael's take?
